Lesson 2.4 · 15 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Application risk: fraud, identity and screening

After this lesson you can:
  • Distinguish credit risk from fraud risk at application time
  • List the screening signals: device, velocity, synthetic identity, negative lists
  • Explain natural justice in fraud classification
On this page
  1. Fraud is not bad credit
  2. Classification carries consequences — so it carries process
  3. Where this lives in LoanOS
  4. Knowledge check

1. Fraud is not bad credit

A credit-risky borrower intends to repay and might fail; a fraudulent applicant never intends to repay, or is not who they claim to be.

The screens differ accordingly.

Application fraud controls look at:

  • Identity integrity — document tampering, face/document mismatch, synthetic identities stitched from real fragments.
  • Behavioural signals — device fingerprints, IP and location anomalies, application velocity (the same device applying for ten lenders in an hour).
  • Linkage — shared bank accounts, addresses, employers or devices across unrelated applicants; mule-account indicators; internal and external negative lists.

Signals combine into a fraud score and policy decision: pass, review or decline-and-investigate.

2. Classification carries consequences — so it carries process

Formally classifying a borrower or account as fraud has severe downstream effects: reporting to the RBI, potential law-enforcement referral, and a long shadow on the person's financial life. The 2024 fraud-risk directions therefore require natural justice: a show-cause process where the person can respond before classification, four-eyes decision-making, committee oversight and documented reporting (FMR/LEA evidence).

In LoanOS fraud handling is a case workflow inside LWS — investigation, response window, committee pack, classification decision — with the audit chain preserving who decided what, on which evidence. Post-disbursement, early-warning signals keep feeding the same machinery.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-FRAUD-2024 — Fraud governance, natural-justice classification, committee oversight and LEA/regulator reporting.
  • RBI-KYC-2016 — Screening and monitoring obligations that catch identity abuse at intake.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability FRD-002 — Device, IP, velocity, location and behavioural signals.

Key terms

Maker-checker LWS

Knowledge check

1. Why does fraud classification require a show-cause step?

  1. To slow down operations
  2. Natural justice: the consequences are severe, so the person must be heard first
  3. To collect more documents
  4. Because insurers demand it
Show answer

B. The fraud directions embed natural justice — classification without a response opportunity is procedurally invalid and reversible.
